state: The decision concerns historical onboarding, not code-schema evolution. A draft language has normal models, locks, policies and steward-authorized scenarios, but no implementation constraint. Evidence populations are P: 2,000 expense records plus 2,000 receipt files; W: 20,000 bookings plus 5,000 invoices with customer/booking relationships. Other accounting, identity and payment systems remain in use. The specified CSV panel accepts no more than 1,000 rows and 10MiB per review, submits each canonical mutation separately, preserves retry identity and reruns configured duplicate checks. Authorized file finalization is mandatory; spreadsheets cannot bestow attachment rights through a path or raw ID. The current Expense operations permit own draft creation, current assigned reviewer decision with now/actor, and finance recording a full evidenced reimbursement after approval. Prior decision actors, times and locked fields are not writable through those inputs. Reserved system metadata cannot be imported. Maintenance backfill requires an installed predecessor rather than accepting external rows. Ordinary source declarations can instead express immutable historical-evidence models and explicit intake permission, with original identifiers and recorded claims, documents and optional verified mappings to present accounts. No absent historic person may be invented or assigned old authority. Preservation includes missing/invalid attachments, conflicting duplicates, per-row failures, uncertain retries and current reader revocation. No provider fidelity or operational savings has been demonstrated. Compare the three complete approaches using the same history, access and continuity needs and including stewardship, retained-system and reconciliation expense.

intake.instructions: Select the approach that best meets these shared evidence and operational obligations.

criteria.domain_intake: Introduce owner-specific intake operations for evidence-backed prior domain states, with current steward permission, verified identities/references and explicit origin metadata. Accepted records participate in domain reporting; their construction must suppress unintended new workflow/provider consequences through declared semantics. Cases lacking required identity/evidence remain outside Can, so mapping effort and a retained source may still be necessary.
criteria.evidence_records: Use existing model/lock/file/policy primitives to store a separately identified historical evidence set in the same business owners. Preserve original names, dates, claimed outcomes and source keys, connecting only verified current identities and record relationships. Do not set live approval/payment flags. The company gains local readable history while carrying explicit incompleteness, reviewed reference/file mapping, storage and archive-versus-live reporting duties.
criteria.retained_source: Keep historical data in its existing service or a securely readable preserved export; provide scoped links while normal canonical operations handle new/current work. This preserves origin without reproducing its past state machine. It still depends on continuing historical access, adequate exports, access administration and cross-system reporting, with any applicable retained fees and support burden.
